question: In geriatric rehabilitation, early mobilisation (within 24–48 hours of medical stabilisation) is associated with better functional outcomes and reduced complications such as pressure sores and deep vein thrombosis compared to bed rest.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. Early mobilisation (24–48 hours post-stabilisation) is a core principle of geriatric rehabilitation — it prevents deconditioning, reduces DVT and pressure sore risk, and improves functional recovery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Early task-specific, high-intensity rehabilitation within 24–48 hours of medical stability is the evidence-based standard. Prolonged bed rest accelerates sarcopenia, increases DVT/pressure sore risk, and worsens functional outcomes.
